title: Asunción founded
description: Juan de Salazar builds a fort on the Paraguay River that becomes the base of Spanish settlement in the Río de la Plata region.

title: Cabeza de Vaca deposed
description: The settlers of Asunción arrest the royal governor Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca and send him to Spain, leaving Domingo Martínez de Irala in charge.

title: First Jesuit reduction
description: The Jesuits found the first of the mission towns in which they gather the Guaraní for a century and a half.

title: Battle of Mbororé
description: Guaraní from the Jesuit missions defeat slave raiders from São Paulo, ending the large raids on the missions.

title: Revolt of the Comuneros
description: The settlers of Asunción depose their governor, beginning fourteen years of resistance to royal authority and the Jesuits.

title: Jesuits expelled
description: Charles III orders the Jesuits out of his dominions, and the Guaraní missions decline.

title: Battle of Paraguarí
polity: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
description: Paraguayan militia defeat the army sent by the junta of Buenos Aires under Manuel Belgrano.

title: Independence
description: Officers in Asunción force the Spanish governor to share power and then remove him, ending Spanish rule without a battle.

title: Francia made dictator
description: A congress names José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia supreme dictator, and he rules an isolated Paraguay until his death in 1840.

title: Independence formally declared
description: A congress formally declares Paraguay independent of every foreign power, including Buenos Aires.

title: Solano López takes power
description: Francisco Solano López succeeds his father Carlos Antonio López as president.

title: Battle of Tuyutí
description: The Paraguayan army loses many of its best troops attacking the allied camp, in the largest battle fought in South America.

title: Battle of Acosta Ñu
description: A Paraguayan force made up largely of boys is destroyed by the Brazilian army, a day now kept as Children's Day in Paraguay.

title: Constitution of 1870
description: A convention meeting under allied occupation adopts a liberal constitution for a country that has lost most of its men.

title: Colorado Party founded
description: Bernardino Caballero founds the Colorado Party, two months after the founding of the rival Liberal Party.

title: Liberal Revolution
description: Liberals invading from Argentina begin a revolt that ends Colorado rule and opens thirty years of Liberal governments.

title: Battle of Boquerón
description: Paraguay retakes the fort of Boquerón from Bolivia in the first major battle of the Chaco War.

title: February Revolution
description: Veterans of the Chaco War overthrow the Liberal government and bring Colonel Rafael Franco to power.

title: Chaco peace treaty
description: Paraguay and Bolivia sign a treaty that gives Paraguay about three quarters of the Chaco.

title: Civil War of 1947
description: A revolt of Liberals, Febreristas and Communists against President Morínigo begins at Concepción and is defeated by August, leaving the Colorado Party in control.

title: Stroessner's coup
description: General Alfredo Stroessner overthrows President Federico Chaves and goes on to rule for 35 years.

title: Itaipu Dam begins generating
description: The first unit of the dam built with Brazil on the Paraná River starts producing electricity, for years the largest hydroelectric plant in the world.

title: Fall of Stroessner
description: General Andrés Rodríguez overthrows Stroessner in a coup and opens the way to elections.

title: Treaty of Asunción
description: Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay sign the treaty that creates the common market Mercosur.

title: Constitution of 1992
description: A democratic constitution limits the president to one term and makes Guaraní an official language beside Spanish.

title: Archives of Terror found
description: Police files found in a suburb of Asunción document the repression under Stroessner and Operation Condor.

title: Assassination of Argaña
description: The killing of Vice President Luis María Argaña sets off protests that force President Raúl Cubas to resign.

title: Lugo elected
description: The former bishop Fernando Lugo wins the presidency, ending 61 years of rule by the Colorado Party.

title: Lugo removed from office
description: The Senate removes President Lugo after an impeachment lasting two days, which neighbouring governments condemn.
